title: Old-time bands: Tosso's concert band, Tom Brown, the Detroit brothers
summary: Allen asks about Tosso's twenty-piece concert band, Brown's military band and the Detroit brothers; Brunies never played with them.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yes, the bass drum with the flip pedal. Yeah. And, uh, we also... I was gonna ask about some of the other bands, the real old time bands. For instance, Emil Tasso's band, Spanish Fork. Did you ever hear that? Who? Tasso? Tasso. What kind of a band was that? That was Tasso, a big concert band. Did you ever play in that? No, no, no. That was all music they used there, yes. All music. Played by music. Was that a pretty big band? How big was it? About 20 men. 20 men. Yeah, sometimes more. How late did they play? About 11 o'clock. I mean, in years. When did they play as late as the First World War? Or when and how long did they play?

Oh, yeah. Before the First World War. Oh, yeah. Before the First World War. Before the First World War. Before the... I had a little stunt coming up. About the 1908's, huh? Grandma and I used to... His mother, I used to take... I was a walking stick. I used to take... She used to take me all around. I'd take all around. Oh, no. What else do you want?
There's another military band. Was it Brown's? Red Brown, yeah.
Well, there's Tom Brown. Tom Brown. Is he living yet? No, he's dead. He's dead, too, yeah. He just died a year ago.
I never did play with him. We never did play with Tom Brown. We were fighting against one of them. A little bit late, a hot stuff. Yeah. So we outgrew them. And... Not a bad thing.
Do you remember the Detroit brothers? Detroit, yeah. Detroit, yeah.
